content.value_statement: Dialog and modal choices can interrupt users or create unclear decisions. This skill helps choose the right Apple HIG presentation pattern and write concise, actionable copy.
actual_capabilities: Compares alerts, action sheets, popovers, sheets, and digit entry views.
Recommends presentation types based on urgency, modality, platform, and user flow.
Provides copy guidance for titles, messages, cancel buttons, and destructive actions.
Explains dismiss behavior, safe cancellation, button placement, and platform differences.
Points to related Apple HIG references and developer APIs for implementation context.
limitations: Does not generate production UI code without project and framework context.
Does not replace current Apple documentation for App Review decisions.
Focuses on Apple platforms and may not fit Android, web, or other design systems.
Uses included reference snapshots, so newer Apple guidance may not be present.

use_cases.title: Choose a Confirmation Pattern
use_cases.description: Decide whether a destructive action needs an alert, action sheet, undo, or inline feedback.

use_cases.title: Review Modal Copy
use_cases.description: Check alert titles, messages, cancel labels, and destructive button placement before implementation.

use_cases.title: Adapt Across Apple Platforms
use_cases.description: Compare how sheets, popovers, and digit entry views should change across Apple devices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dialog Type
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to show [situation]. Recommend the best Apple HIG presentation type and explain why alternatives are weaker.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Alert Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this alert: title [title], message [message], buttons [buttons]. Make it concise and aligned with Apple HIG.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Destructive Action Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: For [destructive action], design the confirmation, cancel path, button labels, and safer alternatives such as undo.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Cross-Platform Modal Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this flow for iPhone, iPad, Mac, watchOS, and tvOS. Recommend presentation changes, dismissal behavior, and platform concerns.

output_examples.input: A user taps Delete Account in settings.
output: Use an alert because the action is destructive and hard to undo.
Use a clear title, a short consequence statement, Cancel, and Delete Account.
Consider adding a recovery path if account deletion is delayed.

output_examples.input: A user cancels a draft message with unsaved changes.
output: Use an action sheet because the user initiated a choice with multiple outcomes.
Offer Save Draft, Delete Draft, and Cancel.
Avoid an alert because it gives fewer action choices.

output_examples.input: A Mac toolbar button opens temporary formatting options.
output: Use a popover if the controls are brief and directly related to the toolbar item.
Save changes when the popover closes automatically.
Use a panel instead if users need repeated input while viewing results.

best_practices: Use the least interruptive pattern that still protects users from serious mistakes.
Keep dialog titles, messages, and buttons short, specific, and action-oriented.
Define dismissal and cancellation behavior before designing the visual presentation.
anti_patterns: Do not use alerts for routine status messages that can appear inline.
Do not stack sheets, popovers, or dialogs in a way that hides user context.
Do not label important confirmation buttons with vague words like OK.

faq.question: Can this skill choose between an alert and a sheet?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares urgency, user intent, modality, and platform to recommend a presentation type.

faq.question: Does it include action sheet guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers intentional choices, destructive actions, cancel options, button counts, and iPad presentation differences.

faq.question: Can it write alert copy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest concise titles, messages, and button labels that follow Apple HIG guidance.

faq.question: Does it support non-Apple platforms?
faq.answer: It focuses on Apple HIG. Use the recommendations carefully when designing for other platforms.

faq.question: Will it fetch current Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It uses included references unless your assistant has separate browsing access.

faq.question: Can it create implementation code?
faq.answer: It can explain related SwiftUI, UIKit, and AppKit APIs, but implementation requires project context.
